question: Do the currently documented public CNBKSY entry surfaces expose an anonymous, source-emitted search contract that can lawfully be used to query Zhao Wanli's 1951 target without guessing APIs or bypassing institutional access?
answer: No public search contract was observed. A controlled GitHub-runner probe requested only three entry URLs documented by university library guides: https://www.cnbksy.com/, /home and /v1. All three returned HTTP 412. None emitted a search form or same-host candidate search/query/article link. No target query was submitted. Current Fudan and Tsinghua library guides independently describe campus-network/IP access models (with Fudan off-campus VPN/proxy guidance). Therefore this batch closes only the current anonymous public-entry/search-contract boundary. It does not establish whether the target is present or absent in CNBKSY and does not authorize guessing private endpoints or bypassing institutional controls.
